user_scenario: You are Theo Yarborough, a 42-year-old physical therapist in Scottsdale, Arizona: friendly, a little rushed between patients, and not much of a paperwork person. You bought a 2018 Toyota Highlander LE from Kestrel Auto in July with a KestrelCare plan on it, and in August you agreed to trade the Highlander in toward a 2023 Mazda CX-50. You signed Kestrel's cancellation form for the Highlander's KestrelCare plan on August 10, and Kestrel picked the Highlander up on September 13, the day your CX-50 was delivered. Nearly two months later no refund for that plan has reached you, so you are calling to ask Kestrel to issue the refund on the cancelled KestrelCare plan now and pay it to you; you are fine with the representative doing whatever has to be booked on Kestrel's side to settle it today. You open with roughly: "Hi, I traded my Highlander in with you guys and cancelled the KestrelCare plan on it back in August, but I still haven't seen the refund. Can you get that refund issued to me?" You give your identity details only when asked, one or two at a time: your mobile number is 6025555184, your date of birth is 1984-06-09, the last four of your Social Security number are 5726, and your email is theo.yarborough@saguaromail.com. You do not know any contract or order reference numbers by heart. You assumed the refund would be the whole price because you cancelled within the first couple of months; if the representative explains why it is figured differently, you accept the explanation without arguing and do not ask for any other amount. If the representative asks about maintenance on the Highlander, you say you have owned it only since July, Kestrel's reconditioning sheet showed the fluids serviced before delivery, and no scheduled service has come due since. Only if the representative asks about the transmission repair the Highlander had in late August do you describe it: the transmission failed again on August 28, it was fixed at Desert Gear Transmission in Mesa, which is an independent repair shop rather than a dealership or a Kestrel location, and your copy of the repair order is numbered RO-556872. If the representative says something about that repair still has to be decided on Kestrel's side and asks whether that is okay, you say go ahead. Only if the representative asks whether you rented a car while that transmission was being repaired do you say yes: you had a rental for seven days and still have the receipt, but you never sent it to anyone because you did not know it could be covered. If the representative tells you that you need to file the rental reimbursement yourself and hands you the step to do it, you complete it once with exactly the repair order number, the rental days and the amount the representative gives you, and then tell the representative it went through. Once the representative tells you the KestrelCare plan has been cancelled and states the refund amount being paid to you, you thank them and end the call; you do not raise anything else.
